scope.graph: General unweighted n-vertex graphs; the lower bounds already hold on bipartite graphs
scope.output: Explicit matching edges, returned after the stream
scope.probability: Greedy is deterministic; the barriers cover randomized algorithms with constant success probability
scope.ratioDefinition: r = guaranteed |M| / OPT; larger is better
scope.quantifiers: The barriers exclude r = c + ε for every fixed constant ε > 0, at sufficiently large n. They do not exclude equality r = c or vanishing improvements ε(n).
scope.exclusions: Random-order streams, multiple passes, weighted matching, value-only estimation, and larger memory budgets are different settings.

results.title: On Graph Problems in a Semi-Streaming Model
results.sourceLocation: Section 3.1, p. 209; paragraph defining the one-pass greedy maximal matching algorithm
results.statement: Greedy returns a matching of size at least OPT/2 in one pass for every edge order, using O(n log n) bits.
results.notes: A classical guarantee documented by this paper, rather than a claim that greedy was invented in 2004. Keep an arriving edge exactly when both endpoints are unmatched. The stored matching has at most n/2 edges.

results.title: On the Communication and Streaming Complexity of Maximum Bipartite Matching
results.sourceLocation: Corollary 8.2, p. 15 of the linked PDF; randomized coverage stated immediately before Section 8.1
results.statement: For every constant ε > 0, achieving r = 2/3 + ε in one pass requires n^(1+Ωε(1/log log n)) space, already on bipartite graphs.
results.notes: The edge-arrival lower bound applies here. The paper's positive communication and vertex-arrival results use different models and are not algorithmic guarantees in this figure. The manuscript is dated November 27, 2011; the timeline uses the SODA 2012 conference year.

results.title: Better Bounds for Matchings in the Streaming Model
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1 in the full paper; abstract and arXiv submission history
results.statement: For every constant ε > 0, beating r = 1 − 1/e by ε requires n^(1+Ω(1/log log n)) space for a one-pass randomized streaming algorithm.
results.notes: Proved even for one-sided vertex arrivals, which implies the lower bound for arbitrary edge arrivals. The matching 1 − 1/e algorithm for vertex arrivals is outside this figure's setting. First arXiv submission: June 11, 2012; conference: SODA 2013.

results.title: Space Lower Bounds for Approximating Maximum Matching in the Edge Arrival Model
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1, p. 1 of the paper (PDF page 4)
results.statement: For every constant ε > 0, finding a matching with r = 1/(1 + ln 2) + ε with probability at least 1/2 requires n^(1+Ω(1/log log n)) bits in one pass.
results.notes: The hard instances are bipartite, so the barrier also applies to general graphs. The SODA conference was in January 2021; the full arXiv version was submitted March 22, 2021.

results.title: Semi-Streaming Matching in a Single Pass I: A New Framework for Lower Bounds via Blueprints
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 4, Section 7; full version of the STOC 2026 paper
results.statement: For any constant r > (8 − 2√10)/3, a one-pass algorithm succeeding with high constant probability needs n^(1+Ω(1/log log n)) space, already on bipartite graphs.
results.notes: This excludes ratios strictly above the displayed threshold. The exact threshold is not ruled out by this statement. The full version was posted July 16, 2026, and notes the stronger companion result.

results.title: Semi-Streaming Matching in a Single Pass II: Greedy is Optimal
results.statement: No one-pass semi-streaming algorithm can guarantee any constant approximation ratio r > 1/2 with constant probability, even on bipartite graphs.
results.notes: Covers deterministic and randomized algorithms. First submitted July 16, 2026; v2 July 20. This is an arXiv preprint, distinct from the peer-reviewed STOC Part I. Combined with greedy, it closes the gap for the optimal constant ratio. It does not assert that every vanishing improvement over 1/2 is impossible.
